probes.question: Hello, I'm Dr Rivera, one of the family doctors at the clinic in Burns. Can you hear and see me alright?
probes.credits: Introduced yourself by name and role

probes.question: When the sleep trouble started, was it mostly getting to sleep, or something else?
probes.target: About a month ago you began to have trouble falling asleep. You often lie awake well past 10, and sometimes later.

probes.question: Once you do drop off, do you stay asleep through the night?
probes.target: When you do finally fall asleep you wake up often, tossing and turning.

probes.question: Is this happening every single night, or just some nights?
probes.target: It happens every night, and it has done every night for the month.

probes.question: What have you already tried to help yourself get to sleep?
probes.target: You have tried everything. You don't watch TV in bed, you don't drink alcohol right before bed, and you have tried reading to help you fall asleep. Nothing has worked.

probes.question: Who's at home with you these days?
probes.target: You live alone. You have been widowed for just over a year.

probes.question: How have your spirits been lately? Have you been feeling low or blue?
probes.target: (only if asked) Your mood is low.
probes.credits: Asked about depression as a cause of the sleeping trouble

probes.question: Sometimes when people feel this worn out, they have thoughts that life isn't worth living, or of hurting themselves or someone else. Has anything like that crossed your mind?
probes.target: (only if asked) You have no thoughts of suicide and no thoughts of harming yourself. You have no thoughts of harming anyone else.
probes.credits: Asked about thoughts of suicide or self harm

probes.question: Have you ever gone through a stretch of days when you felt unusually wound up, full of energy, barely needed any sleep, and your thoughts were going a mile a minute?
probes.credits: Screened for a history of mania

probes.question: Do you have a drink now and then, like beer or wine?
probes.target: You drink three glasses of wine a week, never more.
probes.credits: Asked about alcohol and substance use

probes.question: Is that more or less than you used to drink, say a year or two ago?
probes.target: (only if asked) If the doctor asks whether your drinking has changed: yes, it has gone up. Before your partner died you drank much less. You have drunk three glasses a week for less than a year.

probes.question: Have you taken anything for sleep, from the doctor or from the drugstore?
probes.target: You take no medicines at all, nothing on prescription and nothing over the counter.

probes.question: Have you had any intimate partners since your spouse passed?
probes.target: (only if asked) You were only ever sexually active with your partner. You have had no new partners since they passed away. There is no risk of pregnancy.

probes.question: Do you remember how you answered those forms the assistant had you fill out before we started?
probes.target: (only if asked) You can't really remember what you answered on the forms, but you think the assistant said the doctor can get the results somewhere in the telemedicine room.

probes.question: Has anyone told you that you snore loudly or stop breathing while you sleep?
Do your legs get restless or crawly when you lie down at night?
Are you waking up soaked in sweat at night?
Is there anything else going on in your life that you think I should know about?
Before we wrap up, is there anything you'd like to ask me or anything that's worrying you?
probes.credits: Asked whether there were other questions or concerns
